sources.title: ABOUT – 1981 Inventions
sources.excerpt: 1981 Inventions is a boutique guitar pedal company founded by Matthew Hoopes and co-run with Laura Hoopes; pedals are built in Nashville by Matthew Hoopes and Jack O'Shea. The DRV is described as the company's mainstay distortion pedal.

sources.title: FAQ – 1981 Inventions
sources.excerpt: Current FAQ states standard 9V DC center-negative power for the company's pedals and describes current production as hand assembled/tested in the USA.

sources.title: Interview: Matthew Hoopes of 1981 Inventions
sources.excerpt: Hoopes says the first public DRV run was released late one night in June 2018 and sold out by morning. He describes the DRV as based on a 1985 Whiteface RAT, with a fixed always-on preamp, about one twentieth the gain of a traditional RAT, and changes to low end, midrange, filter sweep, level, switching, LED and filtering.

sources.title: Review: 1981 Inventions DRV
sources.excerpt: Review describes three controls labeled DRV, CUT and VOL, an on/off footswitch and LED, and identifies the 1985 Whiteface RAT as the initial jumping-off point.

sources.title: 1981 Inventions DRV – Effects Database
sources.excerpt: Manufacturer-derived description says the pedal has two circuits, one distortion and one preamp boost, running at 18V via an internal voltage regulator, in a steel enclosure with Switchcraft 11 jacks and a soft-touch relay switching system.

sources.title: Perf and PCB Effects Layouts: 1981 Inventions DRV
sources.excerpt: Third-party circuit/layout reconstruction identifies a tweaked RAT surrounded by two op-amp gain stages and buffered bypass, with the circuit run at 18V. Comments identify the shown clipping diodes as 1N4148 and the voltage doubler around an LT1054.

sources.title: Guitar FX Layouts: 1981 Inventions DRV
sources.excerpt: Technical discussion describes RAT-like hard clipping and tone behavior but notes the DRV does not have the same slew-rate compensation as a RAT.

sources.title: DRV – 1981 Inventions
sources.excerpt: Current DRV collection page is active but primarily surfaces later DRV-family products such as DRV2 and DRV MOD versions rather than a standalone original DRV product page.

sources.title: DRV2 No3 – 1981 Inventions
sources.excerpt: Current manufacturer page distinguishes DRV2 from the original DRV circuit and says the original was engineered by Jon Ashley while the DRV2 was redesigned/engineered by John Snyder of Electronic Audio Experiments.

sources.title: Relient K's Matt Hoopes Found New Success in 1981 Guitar Pedals
sources.excerpt: Hoopes says he owns many Tube Screamers and that a 1981 Tube Screamer was personally important; he also identifies a 1985 RAT as monumental to finishing the DRV. The article says the DRV sold out immediately.
